title: CommonEnums
description: Shared enums and small helpers used across other schemas.

SystemName.description: The driver types of interface version 22 and earlier, which actionData.targetSystem held before device slots (v23, see ActionTarget). Matches the prefix of the device id the action was recorded against: adb for avd:, bluestacks: and adb: devices, kvm for pikvm:, ios for an iPhone or iPad attached by USB (ios:<udid>), and python for the host desktop. Still the engine's device types (DeviceController.device_id_to_device_type).

SlotName.description: A device slot (interface version 23+): a kind plus an index, device0, desktop0, phone1, tablet0... The kind is a hint for what to bind there (device: any; desktop: the host or a PiKVM; phone and tablet: adb or iOS devices). The run binds each slot to a real device. device0 and desktop0, left unbound, are the host's own desktop; every other slot a script lists must be bound when the run starts.

ActionTarget.description: actionData.targetSystem. From interface version 23, the slot the action acts on (SlotName), 'host' (always this controller's own screen, never bound), 'none' (no device) or '' (= device0). Up to version 22, a SystemName driver type; readers migrate those (python and kvm to desktop0, or python to host in a script that mixes python and kvm; adb and ios to phone0).

description.description: A hint for whoever binds the slot: 'the Android phone with the app signed in'.

DeviceBindings.description: A run's device bindings, slot to device id: { "phone0": "avd:Pixel_7", "desktop0": "pikvm:office-pc" }. A value is a device id, 'host' (the host's own desktop) or file:<path> (a still image). The slots host and none cannot be bound.

RunStatus.description: Status reported by ScriptEngine for a running or finished action/script. The first four are ScriptExecutionState values. TIMED_OUT, MAX_ATTEMPTS and CANCELLED come from ScriptExecutionStatusDetail: script_executor.py calls script_logger.get_action_log().set_status(status_detail), which writes the detail into this same field, so a terminated run's node reports why it stopped rather than a bare FAILURE. NEEDS_APPROVAL: the run stopped before reading a secret the caller had not approved (--approved-secrets); needs_approval.json in the run folder names the secret and the step. Readers should treat every value except RUNNING and SUCCESS as a failure-like terminal state.

QueueStatus.description: Status used in Script-Engine-Controller queue files (running_scripts/completed_scripts).

FileType.description: Type of a ScriptActionLog artifact file. overlay is a *.overlay.html log overlay: drawing instructions over a stored screenshot that render to the annotated image (see ScriptEngine common/logging/log_overlay.py).

FilePair.description: ScriptActionLog file reference pair (file_type + file_path). Empty object {} means no file is attached.
